meaning.evidence: Every duty, condition and qualification kept, numbers and dates exact. The gloss "AFGE Council 260, so it's a union job" slightly overstates a bargaining unit position; "no worries:" is colour.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "Get your head around what customers need", "Have a squiz at that announcement", "nutting out production problems", "on your CV", "new starters", "pro rata".

authenticity.evidence: Reads like an Australian job ad: "all the program goals get ticked off", "Know your way around the technical resources", "spot on".

register.evidence: Level 3: conversational and local throughout, without turning the notice into a yarn; no swearing.

tone.evidence: Stays a clear, official-but-friendly job notice; requirements still read as requirements ("You'll need to pass a background check.").

flow.evidence: Mostly smooth; "so they get published legally effective, on time and spot on" is a little ungrammatical.

variety.evidence: Varied; "properly" recurs as in the original ("Handle ... properly", "look after them properly", "use them properly").

problems.original: to ensure legally effective, timely, and accurate publication of them

problems.original: This is a bargaining unit position, AFGE Council 260.

meaning.evidence: The original text with spelling changes and "new starters", so nothing lost or changed.

sense.evidence: The few changes fit: "new starters", "pro rata basis", "specialised".

authenticity.evidence: Hardly any Aussie to judge; spelling is mixed, "Specialized Experience" then "specialised experience" in the same line.

register.evidence: Left essentially untranslated: "Properly manipulate the contents of documents", "Please refer to that announcement". Far under level 3.

flow.evidence: Reads as the original, including its own slip "prior to developed for publication".

B.summary: Essentially untranslated; only spelling and a word or two changed.

meaning.evidence: Every point kept; the clumsy education clause clarified ("2 full years of graduate study, each year at a higher level"). Nothing invented.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "learn the whole box and dice", "all program goals get ticked off", "Have a squiz", "on offer too".

authenticity.evidence: Natural and unforced: "There's the chance to work from home (telework)", "look after it properly".

register.evidence: Level 3, a touch light: several duty lines stay formal ("Understand and properly use the technical resources on hand"). Keeps "résumé" rather than CV.

tone.evidence: Official but approachable, as the original.

variety.evidence: Slang used sparingly, little repetition; "Specialized Experience" heading kept beside "specialised".

C.summary: Faithful, clean and natural; a slightly light level 3.

meaning.evidence: All content kept, plainly reworded; nothing added.

sense.evidence: Fits: "ticked off", "postgrad degree", "new hire" left, "work eligibility".

authenticity.evidence: Plain casual English more than Australian; "You've gotta pass a background check" and "You've gotta meet these requirements" lean American.

register.evidence: Closer to level 2: casual register but little Australian vocabulary beyond "ticked off" and "postgrad".

variety.evidence: "gotta" twice and "Have a look at" twice; little slang to vary.

problems.original: Must successfully complete a background investigation.
problems.why: Gotta reads American; got to would be local.

D.summary: Faithful plain-English rewrite, under the level asked and more casual than Australian.

meaning.evidence: All requirements kept, but additions creep in: "legacy systems (the old clunkers that still have to keep running)", "No way round that one.", "Not the day after.", "so the union's in the picture", "Not bad, ay?".

sense.evidence: Mostly fit ("toe the line on style and formatting", "nutting out", "over the line"), but "leading the pack" for leading others and "Wrangle the contents" strain.

authenticity.evidence: Real idiom, but some stock openers and tags: "Righto", "no dramas", "Not bad, ay?".

register.evidence: Heavier than level 3: chatty asides added to nearly every section.

tone.evidence: An official notice made jokey in places ("Not the day after.", "Not bad, ay?"), undercutting the requirements.

flow.evidence: Readable, but the tag lines interrupt: "You've got to pass a background check. No way round that one."

essence.evidence: Recognisably the announcement, but the asides change its character toward a pitch.
